name: Concede the defensible, isolate the indefensible
definition: Hand the opponent, unprompted and for free, every part of his position he could successfully defend. He is then left holding only the part he cannot, and it is the part he has already stopped mentioning.
mechanism: Removes every exit before a question is asked, and does it without a single accusation. Because the concession is genuine and volunteered, the opponent cannot claim bad faith, and the audience sees generosity rather than attack. The isolated item is usually the thing the opponent abandoned on his own, which is how you identify it.
counterMove: N/A (Clay technique).
source: Named August 1 2026, Case File 007.

name: He's not my audience. He's my prey.
definition: Compressing the predator/prey doctrine into a single declarative line that reframes the relationship between the operator, the hostile commenter, and the actual audience. The commenter is not the person being persuaded. The actual audience is everyone else watching.
mechanism: The line rejects the assumption that hostile commenters are the audience the operator is trying to convince. Once stated, the entire engagement structure flips: the commenter becomes a demonstration target, not a debate partner. The audience watching becomes the actual recipient of the work.
counterMove: N/A (this is a Clay framing, not an opposing move).
source: Named during Lydia Lohrer exchange, May 10, 2026.

name: Make Them The Teacher
definition: When a commenter walks in claiming superiority via snark, treat them as the teacher and ask them to demonstrate. Hospitable framing, Socratic questions, force them to either perform expertise they don't have or concede the snark was hollow.
mechanism: Both exits lose for the opponent. Trying to teach exposes ignorance. Refusing to teach concedes the original move was hollow. The opponent doesn't have a winning move.
counterMove: N/A (this is a Clay technique, not an opposing move).
source: Documented in `Strategy/Comment-Warfare.md`, April 30, 2026.

name: Refuse the temperature
definition: Answer escalating hostility with warmth. The heart emoji, the welcome, the joke, the blessing. Not composure held with effort, an actually friendly register, delivered while he is screaming.
mechanism: Rage needs resistance to work. Give it none and there is nothing to push against, so he escalates alone while the audience watches one man being pleasant and another one shouting. Every further comment costs him and costs you nothing, which is why the move pairs with inviting more of them. It also closes his last exit: he cannot claim he was provoked, because the record shows he wasn't.
counterMove: N/A (Clay technique).
source: Named during Jerry Lee Howell one-shot, August 25 2026.

name: The $10 paywall
definition: When a hostile commenter demands serious engagement, offer it for a price. Charge them ($10 minimum) to receive a substantive response. Include both Stripe and Bitcoin/Lightning options to close anonymity escape routes.
mechanism: Inverts the predator-prey dynamic. The commenter wanted the operator's time. The operator's time is now a paid asset. Three outcomes for the commenter, all losses for them: (1) pay and Clay writes a real response (Clay wins money + content moment), (2) refuse to pay (admits the engagement claim was performance), (3) try to argue without paying (Clay points at the offer and ignores them).
counterMove: N/A (this is a Clay technique, not an opposing move).
source: Named during Jamie Lex Unwin one-shot, May 10, 2026.

name: The Mirror
definition: Accept the accusation as true, then let the audience decide who it describes. You never make the counter-charge yourself, so there is nothing for him to deny.
mechanism: He has already established that the trait is bad and present in the room. Agreeing costs nothing and denies him the argument he came for. Once the category stands unchallenged, the only question left is who fits it, and the audience answers that from the thread in front of them. Because you never named him, there is no accusation to rebut, and objecting out loud would mean identifying himself.
counterMove: N/A (Clay technique).
source: Named during Jerry Lee Howell one-shot, August 25 2026. In use since at least April 2026 under the older rhetorical_moves vocabulary.

name: The Reversal Receipt
definition: Produce the single verifiable fact where the opponent's *own side* behaves in a way that refutes his position, then ask him about it as though you genuinely want help understanding it.
mechanism: The opponent cannot attack the fact without attacking his allies, and cannot attack the question without looking evasive. It is not a counter-argument, it is an invitation to explain an inconsistency he did not know he owned. Hostile framing ruins it. The question must be sincere in tone.
counterMove: N/A (Clay technique).
source: Named during the one-shot-db audit, August 1 2026. Deployed in Case Files 004 and 007.

name: The ball is in your court. Make your move, or don't.
definition: A closing line that hands an opponent a clear choice while signaling that the operator doesn't need them to act. The "or don't" is the kill: it removes the implication that the operator is waiting on or invested in the opponent's response.
mechanism: High-status framing (Adams). Tells the audience the operator is calm, certain, and not chasing. The opponent now has the option but loses leverage if they refuse to engage.
counterMove: N/A (this is a closing technique).
source: Named during Jamie Lex Unwin one-shot, May 10, 2026.

name: The forced choice
definition: Take two claims he has already made that cannot both be true, set them side by side, and make him pick one. He built both, so he can't disown either without conceding something.
mechanism: The power is that it uses only his own material. Nothing imported, nothing interpreted, so there is no premise for him to dispute. Whichever he picks costs him, and refusing to pick is visible to everyone watching. It works best when the two claims serve different jobs for him: one lets him show contempt, the other lets him claim seriousness, and he needs both at the same time.
counterMove: N/A (Clay technique).
source: Named during Spencer Steel one-shot, August 26 2026.

name: Walk to the concrete third party
definition: Replace the abstraction the opponent is defending with one specific human being who pays for it, and put that person in the room.
mechanism: Abstractions are safe to defend; a named person is not. It also reassigns the moral high ground the opponent believes he occupies, because the victim of his position is the very person he claims to be helping. The audience follows the person, not the principle.
counterMove: N/A (Clay technique).
source: Named during the one-shot-db audit, August 1 2026. Deployed in Case File 004. --- ## Future Entries This file gets appended to whenever a new move is named in a takedown. The file is the canonical record. Lost doctrine is lost money.

name: You're making my case for me.
definition: When a hostile commenter doubles down after being diagnosed structurally, name that each new comment strengthens the diagnosis publicly. The comment becomes evidence for the operator's argument, not against it.
mechanism: Reverses the energy of hostile escalation. The opponent thinks they're scoring points. The operator names that they're providing material that proves the original diagnosis. The audience watches the trap close in real time.
counterMove: N/A (this is an operator response to repeated hostile escalation).
source: Named during Jamie Lex Unwin engagement, May 10, 2026. --- ## ⚠️ PROTOCOL DEBT PAID 2026-08-01 The three entries below are Clay's OWN core techniques. They are the spine of Case Files 004 and 006/007 and they were never logged, in violation of the Standing Protocol at the top of this file. Surfaced by the one-shot-db audit, August 1 2026.

name: Aggressive ignorance
definition: Knowing that you do not know, and actively defending the gap. Not the person who lacks the information, the person who is aware he lacks it and pushes back anyway, treating the deficit as a position to be held.
mechanism: It converts a knowledge deficit into defended territory. Once the gap is part of the identity, new information arrives as an attack rather than as information, so every correction strengthens the refusal. Kent framed it as a sixth stage bolted onto the Four Stages of Competence, sitting outside the ladder rather than on it, because the person is not moving toward competence at all. Trish named the reason it cannot be argued with: you cannot be talked out of a position you were never talked into.
counterMove: Do not try to close the gap. It is not open. Name the refusal once for the audience, then leave. Kent: "a man convinced against his will, is of the same opinion still." Any further attempt to expose it only feeds the rage, which is the point of the posture.
status: Member-contributed. Coined by Kent W. in the Guild.
source: Coined by Kent W. in the Guild thread "Cynefin and Predicting" (Trish, 2026-07-25), expanded on request. Logged 2026-08-06.

name: Argument from ignorance
definition: Treating absence of evidence as evidence of absence. In comment context, claiming a fact "hasn't been shown" and using that as a substitute for "isn't true."
mechanism: Lets the speaker default to their preferred narrative whenever an investigation is incomplete or a fact hasn't been confirmed by an authoritative-sounding source. Effectively converts "we don't yet have an official press release" into "the opposite is true."
counterMove: Force a question about the evidentiary standard. What evidence WOULD count? Then point out the public reporting that has already met that standard.
source: Named during Marek Wiechula one-shot, May 9, 2026.

name: Asymmetric demand
definition: Apply pressure to one side of an exchange while leaving the other side untouched. Demand that the operator soften their response while not asking the original attacker to retract or modify the attack.
mechanism: Disguised as concern for fairness or values, but functionally serves to disarm the operator while protecting the attacker. The asymmetry exposes the move's actual purpose: shutting down the response, not addressing the underlying offense.
counterMove: Name the asymmetry explicitly. "You're not asking him to change his post. You're asking me to soften my response to him." Once the asymmetric demand is named, its purpose becomes visible to the audience.
status: Clay-original framing of an observed pattern (related to concern trolling generally)
source: Named during Karen Monasky one-shot, May 10, 2026.

name: Burden inflation
definition: Restating an opponent's narrow, evidenced point as a sweeping claim about an entire group, then demanding proof of the version he never made. You said her list omitted victims. She asks you to prove Democrats don't care about victims. Whatever you produce will look thin, because it was never asked to carry that much.
mechanism: It moves the goalposts outward while appearing to ask a fair question. A narrow observation is easy to defend and hard to attack, so the move swaps it for a claim about an entire group's motives, which no amount of evidence can fully settle. Every example produced is then met with "that's one person" or "that's not all of them." The demand looks like a request for rigour and functions as an escape from the point that was actually made.
counterMove: If you can carry the inflated burden, carry it. One specific case with a name, a date and a quote in it ends the move on the spot. If you can't, say which claim you actually made and put that one back in front of them.
status: Clay-original framing of an observed pattern
source: Named during Jaime Jameson one-shot, August 2026.

name: Category collapse
definition: Pretending two phenomena belong in the same statistical or moral bucket when they categorically don't.
mechanism: Allows comparison and aggregation of incomparable things to produce a numerically advantageous narrative.
counterMove: Name the categories explicitly. Force the speaker to defend the equivalence rather than smuggle it.
source: Named during Marek Wiechula one-shot, May 9, 2026.

name: Decency disclaimer
definition: Opening a hostile comment with a single sentence acknowledging the moral wrongness of an act being discussed, in order to license the contempt and rationalization that follows in the rest of the comment.
mechanism: The disclaimer functions as cover charge. Once paid, the speaker has rhetorical license to spend the rest of the comment doing what the disclaimer was supposed to forbid. The audience reads the disclaimer first, registers "this person is reasonable," and then under-weights the contempt that follows.
counterMove: Name the disclaimer-as-license operation directly. Revoke the license explicitly. Tell the speaker and the audience that a single moral concession at the top of a comment doesn't immunize what follows.
status: Clay-original framing of an observed pattern
source: Named during Dave Silva one-shot, May 9, 2026.

name: Endorsement-with-deniability
definition: Saying the quiet part of a position out loud while wrapping it in a joke, a "list" observation, a hypothetical, or some other softening container, so the speaker can deny endorsement if challenged.
mechanism: Lets the speaker advocate for a position to sympathetic audiences who read past the wrapper, while preserving deniability with hostile audiences who'd flag the unwrapped version. The wrapper is the alibi. The position is the message.
counterMove: Strip the wrapper. Read the sentence aloud with the alibi removed. Make the speaker defend the unwrapped version or admit the wrapper was the point.
status: Clay-original framing (related to plausible deniability in political communication)
source: Named during Dave Silva one-shot, May 9, 2026.

name: Four-step retreat
definition: A four-step rhetorical pattern observed in credentialed figures like Steven Pinker when challenged on an unpopular position. Step 1: concede the steel-man. Step 2: shift to style critique. Step 3: pivot to political context. Step 4: redirect to a softer target.
mechanism: Allows the figure to appear thoughtful and reasonable while never actually defending or revising their original position. Each step retreats further from the original challenge while preserving the illusion of engagement. Particularly common in academic and prestige-class discourse.
counterMove: Map the four steps explicitly when you see them. Force engagement on the original challenge. Don't let the retreat sequence run.
source: Banked from earlier session work on Pinker. name: Grave-spit
definition: Insulting a recently murdered or deceased public figure under cover of a prior decency disclaimer.
mechanism: Pairs with and depends on the decency disclaimer. The disclaimer provides the moral cover. The grave-spit delivers the contempt the speaker actually came to deliver. Without the disclaimer, the contempt would read as crude. With it, the contempt reads as honest assessment.
counterMove: Hold the speaker's two sentences side by side. Force them to defend why a man whose murder shouldn't be justified deserves to be called a dip-shit one breath later.
source: Named during Dave Silva one-shot, May 9, 2026.

name: Intentions as evidence
definition: Answering a question about outcomes by listing the goals your side holds. The list is offered as though wanting a thing were proof of having produced it.
mechanism: It substitutes motive for result, and the audience rarely notices because the motives named are genuinely sympathetic. Healthcare, food for children, education. Disputing the list sounds like disputing the goods, so the opponent either concedes the frame or attacks the intentions and looks monstrous. The question about what actually happened never comes back.
counterMove: Don't argue with the list. Accept every item on it, then point at what it leaves out, or walk the question to one named person who paid the price.
status: Clay-original framing of an observed pattern
source: Named during Jaime Jameson one-shot, August 2026.

name: Narrative laundering
definition: Running a multi-claim script designed to launder a smear into common sense. Each individual claim may be cherry-picked or partially true, but the aggregation creates a tidy conclusion the speaker brought into the room before the conversation started.
mechanism: The aggregation does the work the individual claims couldn't do alone. The speaker is performing a script handed to them by upstream sources (legacy media framings, partisan talking points), not constructing an argument from independent reasoning.
counterMove: Name the script and the upstream source. Treat the speaker as a downstream agent performing the laundering, not as an independent thinker. Walk through each sub-claim, expose the move underneath, then loop back to name the laundering operation as a whole.
status: Clay-original framing (related to motivated reasoning literature)
source: Named during Marek Wiechula one-shot, May 9, 2026.

name: Performed indifference
definition: Declaring something beneath your notice while demonstrating at length that it isn't. "Charlie Kirk didn't matter," from a man ten hours into an argument about Charlie Kirk. The dismissal is offered as a verdict and refuted by the act of delivering it.
mechanism: It lets him attack without conceding the target is worth attacking. If the thing were admitted to matter, his contempt would need reasons. Declared trivial, contempt is all that's required. It also protects him from losing, since by his own account nothing was at stake. The move fails the moment somebody counts the hours, because the effort is public, permanent, and he spent it himself.
counterMove: Don't argue that it mattered. Count what he built. The hours, the comment count, the time on the clock. His own participation is the refutation and he cannot withdraw it.
status: Clay-original framing of an observed pattern
source: Named during Jerry Lee Howell one-shot, August 25 2026.

name: Quote weaponization
definition: Taking a quote out of context, paraphrasing it inaccurately, or attributing a position to a person that they didn't actually hold, then using the misframed version as retroactive justification for the speaker's argument.
mechanism: Turns the misquoted figure into a participant in the speaker's argument by force, regardless of what they actually said. Especially powerful when the misquoted figure is dead and can't correct the record.
counterMove: Source the actual verbatim quote with date and event. Show the speaker either knew and misrepresented or didn't bother to verify. Either reading damages them.
status: Common rhetorical practice, no specific academic term
source: Named during Joseph Jimmy Hardcastle and Dave Silva one-shots, May 9, 2026.

name: Rationalization pivot
definition: Using a small connector phrase ("on the other hand," "but consider," "meanwhile") to smuggle a moral-equivalence move that converts one death or wrong from "tragedy nobody can justify" into "deserving consequence."
mechanism: The connector phrase does load-bearing work the speaker would have to defend if stated outright. The pivot lets them assert the equivalence without arguing for it. Listeners often process the connector as innocuous transitional language and don't notice the moral re-categorization happening underneath.
counterMove: Name the pivot phrase and the work it's doing. Force the speaker to defend the equivalence explicitly rather than smuggle it via transition.
status: Clay-original framing (related to whataboutism and false equivalence)
source: Named during Dave Silva one-shot, May 9, 2026.

name: Reframing 101
definition: Take an opponent's strategic choice and reframe it as evidence of weakness or failure. Convert their refusal-to-engage into "admission of failure," their measured response into "weakness," their high-ground move into "avoidance."
mechanism: Lets the speaker reverse the moral weight of the opponent's behavior. The opponent's strength becomes their weakness in the new frame. Especially effective when the audience hasn't seen the opponent's choice as strategic.
counterMove: Name the move directly ("Reframing 101"). Refuse the inversion explicitly. Re-anchor the original frame. Walk away. Don't relitigate.
status: Established rhetorical concept (frame inversion / strategic redefinition)
source: Named during Jamie Lex Unwin one-shot, May 10, 2026.

name: Selective characterization
definition: Picking the one trait of a complicated person that fits your narrative and amputating the rest.
mechanism: Reduces a multi-dimensional figure to a single label that supports the speaker's argument while eliminating contradicting evidence.
counterMove: Drop the rest of the picture into the comment. Force the speaker to either acknowledge they edited it or look like they didn't know.
source: Named during Marek Wiechula one-shot, May 9, 2026.

name: The Unproduced Receipt
definition: Declaring the evidence obvious, universal and already seen, so that disagreement can only be stupidity or bad faith. It's all on video. Nobody ever has to produce the video.
mechanism: It converts a factual dispute into a test of the other person's character. Once the proof is established as common knowledge, producing it becomes unnecessary and asking for it becomes suspicious. The audience is handed a shortcut: they don't have to weigh anything, only decide who is honest. And because the evidence is never specified, there is nothing to check, nothing to contest, and no version of it that can be shown to be thin.
counterMove: Ask for it. One clip, one timestamp, one quote. The move dies the moment someone has to produce the thing that was supposedly obvious, and the refusal to produce it does more damage than the clip ever would have.
status: Clay-original framing of an observed pattern
source: Named during Jerry Lee Howell one-shot, August 2026.

name: Volunteered victimhood
definition: Supplying the accusation yourself, unprompted, and then answering as its victim. Nobody said you were evil. You said it, wore it, and replied to it, which means the question that was actually asked never gets touched.
mechanism: The move converts a question into an attack and the speaker into the party under attack. Once the frame is victim and aggressor, the burden flips. The operator is expected to justify a charge he never made, while the original question sits unanswered behind the new argument. It works because the audience arrives after the accusation is already in the thread and can't tell who put it there.
counterMove: Say plainly that nobody made the accusation, and name who introduced it. Then restore the original question in the same breath so the audience can see it is still standing.
status: Clay-original framing of an observed pattern
source: Named during Jaime Jameson one-shot, August 2026.
